title: Calibrating Sentinel-2 Chlorophyll-A Against a Decade of Coastal Monitoring in the South Adriatic Sea
content: Sentinel-2 can map chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) in coastal waters at 10–60 m resolution. Regional retrievals, however, rely on calibration against in-situ monitoring data. Testing if those data represent the water column and the wider sea is rarely tested. We calibrated a blue/green band-ratio retrieval for the South Adriatic Sea against 230 matchups from 24 monitoring stations (2015–2024). We then used 567 in-situ profiles and 40 monthly composites to test where the calibration applies. Leave-one-station-out skill was modest (0.27 in open water, 0.12 in coastal water) and did not depend on spatial resolution, overpass time gap, wind or cloud cover. In summer, in profiles reaching ≥ 40 m, the satellite-visible layer held 27% of column Chl-a, and 95% of profiles had a subsurface maximum below it. This vertical structure explained a seasonal retrieval bias, with median log residuals of +0.58 in winter and −0.55 in summer. Calibrating against optically weighted Chl-a halved the summer bias without loss of skill. The calibration stations sampled water richer in Chl-a than about 94% of the domain. Monthly composites agreed with independent in-situ data in open water (Spearman ρ = 0.45) but not in coastal water. All results are openly available through a WebGIS interface.
